title: Excel: Copilot Agent Mode editing for workbooks stored on the device
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, existing privacy controls and licensing statements are supported. It distinguishes the planned local-file extension from the documented Excel editing capability and leaves feature-specific rollout and processing details open.

claims.quote: giving users the flexibility to use multi-step editing capabilities with Copilot in Excel no matter whether files are stored locally or in the cloud.

claims.claim: Copilot honours users' usage rights for data encrypted by Microsoft Purview Information Protection.
claims.quote: When you have data that's encrypted by Microsoft Purview Information Protection, Microsoft Copilot honors the usage rights granted to the user.

claims.claim: That encryption can be applied by sensitivity labels or Information Rights Management.
claims.quote: This encryption can be applied by sensitivity labels or by restricted permissions in apps in Microsoft 365 by using Information Rights Management (IRM).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; front matter: changes
claims.claim: Copilot honours the same protections when a labelled or encrypted file on local storage is open in an Office app.
claims.quote: When a labeled or encrypted file stored outside Microsoft 365 (for example, on local storage, a network share, or another cloud service) is open in an Office app, Copilot honors the same protection settings.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyse content makes Copilot unavailable in Excel on current Windows, Mac, iOS and Android apps.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps: ... Excel ... This applies to ... Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.claim: Group Policy Management provides the analyse-content policy under User Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Office 2016 > Privacy > Trust Center.
claims.quote: If you're using the Group Policy Management tool, all these policy settings are located under User Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Office 2016\Privacy\Trust Center. ... Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content

claims.claim: Setting registry value UserContentDisabled to 2 disables the analyse-content policy.
claims.quote: | Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content | UserContentDisabled | 1=Enabled  2=Disabled |

claims.claim: These privacy policies can also be implemented through Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: These policy settings can be implemented by using either Group Policy or Cloud Policy.

claims.claim: Mac uses the com.microsoft.office preference OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference, with FALSE disabling it.
claims.quote:
| **Preference Domain** | `com.microsoft.office` |
| **Key** | `OfficeExperiencesAnalyzingContentPreference` |
| **Data Type** | Boolean |
| **Possible values** | `TRUE`*(enabled)*`FALSE`*(disabled)* |

claims.claim: Setting the Mac analyse-content preference to FALSE makes Copilot unavailable in certain apps.
claims.quote: If you set this preference to FALSE, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in certain apps.

claims.claim: Copilot requires a Microsoft Entra ID work or school account.
claims.quote: Users must have a work or school account in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: No identity or security mechanism change is documented specifically for this item.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot" "Excel" "local files" "Graph" "settings"; "Copilot" "Excel" "local" "processing". Read requirements, privacy and data-protection architecture; no item-specific identity change is documented.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.

To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
